current.notes: v3 adds deletion for one-file-per-item primitives. ChangedIds<I> gains remove(id) (drops the id from the pending-write set and records it as removed) and take_removed() -> Vec<I>; is_empty() is false while anything is pending or removed. Delta gains `memory_removed: Vec<MemoryId>` (filled by take_dirty from memory_changed.take_removed(); Delta::full carries none). JsonStore::apply unlinks the note file for each removed id after writing changed notes; the file is found by id under memory/ because the note is already gone from state; a missing file is not an error. To wire memory_delete: MemoryBook::remove(id) (memory agent), State::memory_delete { let note = inner.memory.remove(...)?; inner.memory_changed.remove(note.id); } and a tool that returns ok/not_found. Also in v3: Snapshot.load_errors (see contract "Load errors") and State::load_errors().

history.notes: Storage rework (storage-claude) replaces whole-snapshot-per-call writes with per-primitive deltas written by one background persister task. Snapshot stays as the load/dashboard shape. To add a primitive X with a committed JSONL file: (1) Snapshot gets `x: Vec<X>`; (2) Inner gets `x: XBook` and `x_log: LogCursor`; (3) Delta gets `x: Log<X>` built in `take_dirty` via `x_log.take(&x.items())`; (4) store.rs gets `const X_FILE` and one `write_log(&self.dir.join(X_FILE), &delta.x)?` line in `apply` plus `read_jsonl` in `load`. Mutations that append call `inner.x_log.appended()` implicitly (cursor compares lengths); in-place edits (like notice ack) call `inner.x_log.mark_rewrite()`. Tool handlers do not touch the persister beyond `finish`, which flushes only when state is dirty. Wait for notice "incremental persistence landed" before editing state.rs/store.rs/server.rs.

history.notes: v2: adds the per-file pattern (used by contracts and by the memory primitive) next to the JSONL log pattern. Two ways to persist a primitive. (A) JSONL log (notices, decisions): Inner holds `x_log: LogCursor`; Delta carries `x: Log<X>`; store calls `write_log`. In-place edits call `x_log.mark_rewrite()`. (B) One file per item (contracts, memory): Inner holds `x_changed: ChangedIds<XId>`; Delta carries `x: Vec<X>` with only the changed items; store writes each item to its own file with `write_atomic` and loads by scanning the directory. Every mutation calls `inner.x_changed.mark(id)`; there is no rewrite-all for per-file primitives. Memory glue (memory agent adds after my notice): Snapshot `memory: Vec<MemoryNote>`; Inner `memory: MemoryBook`, `memory_changed: ChangedIds<MemoryId>`; Delta `memory: Vec<MemoryNote>` built via `memory_changed.take(inner.memory.notes(), |n| n.id)`; store `apply`: for each note write_atomic(dir/memory/<slug>-<short>.md, note.to_markdown()); `load`: scan dir/memory/*.md with MemoryNote::from_markdown; `Delta::full` includes all notes. Snapshot is no longer cloned on the request path; only the dashboard poll (every 2s) and write_snapshot (tests/full rewrite) clone it, so keeping bodies in memory is fine. Deletion is not in the seam; if memory needs delete, add `removed: Vec<MemoryId>` to Delta and ChangedIds when you get there.
